chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) about the daughters of a daughter and a grandfather. He said, 'For the grandfather is one-sixth, and the remainder is for the daughters of the daughter.'
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narred that this report, namely the report of Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf, is among those upon which the Ta'ifah has agreed to act in opposition to it.

key_terms.الطَّائِفَةُ: The Ta'ifah (referring to the Shia scholarly community)
key_terms.بَنَاتِ بِنْتٍ: Daughters of a daughter (female descendants through the female line)

ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance share of a grandfather when competing with the daughters of a daughter?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details a specific inheritance ruling where the paternal grandfather receives one-sixth and the daughters of the daughter take the residue. Although the chain is sound, Shaykh al-Tusi notes that the Shia scholarly community (*al-Ta'ifah*) has agreed to act in opposition to this report, highlighting a key instance of *khilaf al-ijma'* (disagreement with consensus) in Shia jurisprudence. This reflects the nuanced approach of Shia scholars in accepting individual reports while prioritizing established communal practice or stronger evidences in cases of conflict.
